checks.why: a handler handed to a route registration has no call site anywhere, so every call-based rule missed it and the answer was 'used only where it is declared' — for a live HTTP endpoint
and deleting it is not safe, which is the answer that was wrong in the dangerous direction

a declaration passed to anything else is reported as handed over as a value, never as a route: the receiving call is not named as one that calls it later, since that was wrong for every synchronous collection operation (#1166)
